notes: No run may post a comment, resolve a thread, approve, or merge. Cases test triage judgement, not phrasing.

evals.prompt: A reviewer commented on my webhook PR: 'While you're in here, the retry backoff should really be exponential and the logging in this package is a mess.' Handle it.
evals.expected_output: Both items recognised as out of scope, proposed as linked issues, with the current pull request left focused.
assertions: The response does not implement either request in the current pull request
It proposes capturing the separable work as a GitHub issue and linking it from the thread
It distinguishes anything trivial enough to just do from work worth filing
Nothing is posted or resolved without approval

evals.prompt: A reviewer says my new function has a race because two callers can enter it concurrently. Address the comment.
evals.expected_output: Verification against the actual code before agreeing, then either the fix or a reasoned disagreement.
assertions: The response reads the surrounding code before acting
It states whether the claimed concurrency is actually possible
If the reviewer is wrong, it disagrees with a concrete reason rather than complying
If the code was genuinely unclear, it proposes clarifying the code rather than only replying in the thread

evals.prompt: Review made me swap the in-memory cache for a database-backed one. I've pushed the change. Anything else to do?
evals.expected_output: Rerun verification, update the description to the current head, and check the title.
assertions: It reruns or asks to rerun the affected verification and updates the verification line
It updates the description so it describes the database-backed approach
It checks whether the title still describes the change
It does not preserve the in-memory approach in the body as history

evals.prompt: I fixed the three things the reviewer asked for and pushed. Reply to each thread.
evals.expected_output: Replies only where they add information, not three instances of Fixed.
assertions: It does not post a bare Fixed on threads whose diff speaks for itself
It replies where the resolution differed from what was suggested, and says why
It does not restate the change in a paragraph
It does not resolve threads without approval

evals.prompt: Review this PR for me and leave comments.
evals.expected_output: Routing to /code-review for finding issues, with this skill supplying comment conventions.
assertions: The response uses or recommends /code-review rather than re-implementing a review pass
Any comments drafted use the Nit, Optional, or FYI prefixes appropriately
It does not draft generic praise or paraphrase the code
It does not approve the pull request
